title: Boundary focusing in fresh two-dimensional MaNGA baryonic and kinematic maps
hypothesis: A universal vector or tensor response to resolved baryonic-light boundaries redirects the effective gravitational field enough to predict the signed axial bending of fresh stellar kinematic maps, modulo the unobservable spin direction, beyond zero photometric-kinematic misalignment and strong ordinary structural and photometric-boundary controls; the same selected field must transfer without reselection to ionized-gas kinematics.

discovery_policy.universal_gravity_track: Require one unchanged boundary-field operator and universal parameters to predict held-out stellar axial bending beyond zero alignment and strong ordinary controls, transfer without reselection to H-alpha where available, preserve local continuity, and remain eligible for later conservation and light-propagation gates.
discovery_policy.phenomenon_publication_track: Retain a reproducible held-out relation between response-blind continuum-boundary geometry and kinematic-axis bending beyond strong ordinary controls even if it cannot be a complete gravity theory.

theory_sources.boundary: Known density-dependent gravitational-permittivity theory in which field lines can refract across density structure; the tested 2-D interface operator is not the published field solution.
Known covariant scalar-tensor completion of refracted gravity; this experiment does not implement or test that complete theory.
Known nonspherical modified-Poisson control emphasizing that admissible gravitational fields remain conservative; used to distinguish the explicit circulation stress test.
Known full modified-Poisson calculation for nonspherical disks; no candidate in this experiment is claimed to be a QUMOND solution.

independence.rule: Inherit only Item 30's response-blind predecessor-vetoed predictors; exclude every Item 30 and Item 31 exploration or confirmation role before disk-quality cuts, roles, folds, MAPS downloads, or pixel access.

sample.stratification: median response-blind stellar mass crossed with median response-blind Sersic index after predecessor, SNR, disk-profile, and inclination cuts; 12 selected per cell with two sealed confirmations

map_source.boundary_normalization: gradient magnitude of Gaussian-smoothed log1p(flux/median_positive_flux), divided by its positive median over 0.2-1.5 Re and clipped to [0,10]
map_source.radial_unit_vector: normalized image-plane gradient of the frozen SPX_ELLCOO R/Re map
map_source.source_weight: square root of positive continuum flux times the valid-source mask

response.stellar_model: weighted least squares v=c0+c1*cos(theta)+s1*sin(theta) on one best-IVAR spaxel per unique stellar bin in each frozen annulus
response.halpha_model: weighted least squares v=c0+c1*cos(theta)+s1*sin(theta) on valid H-alpha spaxels in each frozen annulus
response.response_angle: wrap to [-90,90) degrees of atan2(s1,c1), an axial kinematic bend relative to the photometric major axis; galaxy spin sign is not predicted or scored

candidate_generator.algorithm: PCG64 permutation of an exact mixed-radix grammar with 65536 raw cells in each of four vector/tensor niches and matched polarity

niches.operator: delta_a_t proportional to activated boundary-normal tangential component n_t
delta_a_t proportional to activated 2 n_r n_t anisotropic normal tensor
delta_a_t proportional to the activated tangential component of the 90-degree-rotated boundary normal, equivalent to the radial component of the unrotated boundary normal
delta_a_t proportional to activated curvature-anisotropy-weighted principal-ridge direction

equivalence_boundaries: Interface refraction is a known-family effective projection and not a discovery of refracted gravity.
The normal-tensor branch combines standard anisotropic-medium mathematics with baryonic boundaries; historical novelty is not claimed.
The circulation branch is an explicit nonconservative stress test and cannot pass the universal-gravity track without an action or additional degree of freedom restoring conservation.
The Hessian-ridge branch is only a potentially new synthesis; historical novelty and non-equivalence to all anisotropic modified-Poisson theories are unresolved.
Raw cells are not independent laws; adversarial behavioral equivalence classes are counted separately and provenance labels never prune.

evaluation.baseline_structural: fixed ridge on response-blind mass size surface-density Sersic axis-ratio color redshift SNR and annulus
evaluation.baseline_flexible: fixed ridge adding response-blind continuum multipoles asymmetry boundary curvature centroid terms squares and selected interactions
